actions.text: Confirm the probable misalignment by measuring vibration in the horizontal, vertical, and axial directions on the motor and pump bearings.
Check the alignment using a laser tool to ensure the parallel offset is within 0.05 mm and the angular offset is within 0.05 mm/100 mm.
Stop the pump, lock out the motor supply at the motor control centre, and attach a personal lock and tag before checking the coupling.
Examine the coupling element for wear, check the foundation bolts for 120 N·m torque, and verify there is no soft foot under the motor feet.
After correcting the alignment, run the pump for 1 hour and verify that vibration and bearing temperatures decrease.

escalate_if.text: Call the maintenance manager and change over to the standby pump if the vibration velocity reaches the alarm limit of 6.4 mm/s or if the checks confirm a fault that cannot be corrected during operation.

actions.text: Confirm the probable bearing wear fault with checks from section 8 before doing corrective work.
Measure the vibration velocity and acceleration on both bearing housings with a hand-held meter.
Stop the pump and lock out the motor supply at the main switchboard, attaching a personal lock and tag.
Close and lock the suction and discharge valves, then release the pressure through the drain valve until the gauge shows zero.
Ensure the sea-suction valve is closed and held, keeping a blank flange and a bilge pump ready before opening any part below the waterline.

actions.text: Make sure that the basin level is above the minimum mark and that the make-up water valve operates.
Vent the pump casing through the vent cock.
Before opening the pump, stop it, lock out the motor supply, close and lock the suction and discharge valves, and release the pressure through the drain valve.
Start the standby pump CW-1 from the local panel and wait until its discharge pressure is stable, then ensure the process cooling-water temperature stays within its limits for 5 minutes.
Record the alert, the checks performed, and the result in the maintenance system.

actions.text: Confirm the probable bearing wear fault with checks from section 8 before doing corrective work.
Measure the vibration velocity and acceleration on both bearing housings with a hand-held meter.
Stop the pump and lock out the motor supply at the main switchboard, attaching a personal lock and tag.
Close and lock the suction and discharge valves, then release the pressure through the drain valve until the gauge shows zero.
Ensure the sea-suction valve is closed and held, keeping a blank flange and a bilge pump ready before opening any part below the waterline.

events.summary: Pump PUMP-08 shows a probable BEARING_WEAR fault with a 0.98 probability, supported by a 16.7% increase in the crest factor and an 8.6% rise in vibration acceleration. Measured values deviating significantly from the baseline include suction pressure (-17.5%), discharge pressure (-4.4%), motor power (-2.1%), vibration velocity (-7.2%), fluid temperature (-10.9%), and ambient temperature (+1.2%). Note: The system also indicates a 1.00 probability for SUCTION_STRAINER_CLOGGING, but no advice is provided as per system constraints.

PUMP-09|MISALIGNMENT.a: The permitted parallel offset is 0.05 mm. The permitted angular offset is 0.05 mm per 100 mm. [9.3]
A high axial vibration supports misalignment [9.2]. You must measure vibration in the horizontal, vertical, and axial directions to confirm [4.3].

PUMP-09|MISALIGNMENT.q: What torque do the foundation bolts need?
PUMP-09|MISALIGNMENT.a: The foundation bolts require a torque of 120 N·m [9.4].

PUMP-09|IMBALANCE.a: Scale or deposits on the impeller, a damaged vane, or a loose part on the shaft can cause imbalance [10.2].

PUMP-09|IMBALANCE.q: To which grade do I balance the impeller?
PUMP-09|IMBALANCE.a: You must balance the impeller to grade G6.3 [10.3].

PUMP-09|IMBALANCE.q: Must I stop the pump now?
PUMP-09|IMBALANCE.a: No, you do not need to stop the pump immediately. You must first confirm the imbalance fault by checking the applicable sections before doing any corrective work [4.3]. If the suction pressure decrease exceeds 15%, you should escalate to the maintenance manager and switch to the standby pump [3.6]. If the fault is confirmed and requires repair, you must stop the pump and lock out the motor supply before opening it [2.1].

PUMP-08|SUCTION_STRAINER_CLOGGING.q: Can I clean the strainer while the pump runs?
PUMP-08|SUCTION_STRAINER_CLOGGING.a:
Yes, you can clean the strainer on PUMP-08 while the pump runs.
Follow section 5.4 to change over to the clean basket using the changeover lever.
Then isolate, drain, and open the clogged side as described in sections 2.1 through 2.3.
Ensure the suction pressure returns to normal values after cleaning [5.6].
If the strainer clogs again within 24 hours, check the sea chest grating for debris [5.7].

PUMP-08|SUCTION_STRAINER_CLOGGING.q: When must I clean the strainer?
PUMP-08|SUCTION_STRAINER_CLOGGING.a: You must clean the strainer on PUMP-08 if the suction pressure is more than 15% below the normal value at the same speed [5.3]. You should also clean it if the pressure difference across the strainer exceeds 20 kPa [5.3].

PUMP-08|SUCTION_STRAINER_CLOGGING.q: What do I check after I clean the strainer?
PUMP-08|SUCTION_STRAINER_CLOGGING.a: After cleaning the strainer on PUMP-08, you must verify that the suction pressure and the pump speed return to their normal values [5.6]. If the strainer clogs again within 24 hours, you should examine the sea chest grating for marine growth or debris [5.7].

PUMP-08|BEARING_WEAR.q: Which grease do I use, and how much?
PUMP-08|BEARING_WEAR.a: Use 25 g of lithium-complex grease for each bearing. Apply this every 2000 running hours. Do not over-grease, as it increases the temperature. [8.4]

PUMP-08|BEARING_WEAR.q: When must I replace the bearings?
PUMP-08|BEARING_WEAR.a: You must plan a bearing replacement for PUMP-08 if the vibration velocity exceeds the alarm limit of 5.0 mm/s [3.1]. You must also plan replacement if the bearing temperature increases by more than 10 °C above the normal value [8.5].

PUMP-08|BEARING_WEAR.q: What do I check after a bearing replacement?
PUMP-08|BEARING_WEAR.a: After replacing the bearings on PUMP-08, you must run the pump for 2 hours. During this time, record the vibration and the bearing temperature to verify the repair. Ensure the alignment is correct before starting this test, as misalignment can cause vibration at one and two times the running speed. If the vibration velocity exceeds the alarm limit or the temperature rises significantly, you may need to plan another replacement.

PUMP-09|SENSOR_STUCK.q: How do I check the sensor?
PUMP-09|SENSOR_STUCK.a: To check the sensor, compare the flow meter reading with an independent local gauge or hand-held instrument [4.4]. You can also compare the bearing temperature with an infrared thermometer [13.3]. If the sensor is wrong, mark it as faulty in the monitoring system [13.4]. Until the sensor is repaired, read the local gauge each shift and write the value in the shift log [13.6].

PUMP-09|SENSOR_STUCK.q: Can I disable the trip of this sensor?
PUMP-09|SENSOR_STUCK.a: No, you cannot disable the trip without permission. [13.4] You must get permission from the maintenance manager before disabling any trip that uses this sensor.

PUMP-09|SENSOR_STUCK.q: What do I do until the sensor is repaired?
PUMP-09|SENSOR_STUCK.a:
Until the sensor is repaired, read the local gauge each shift and write the value in the shift log [13.6].
If the measured value reaches an alarm limit of section 3, call the maintenance manager and change over to the standby pump [4.6].
If the checks confirm a fault you cannot correct during operation, also call the maintenance manager and change over to the standby pump [4.6].

PUMP-08|COMMUNICATION_LOSS.q: Does this alert mean that the pump has a fault?
PUMP-08|COMMUNICATION_LOSS.a:
No, this alert does not confirm that PUMP-08 has a fault. [4.3]
The system indicates a probable communication loss, which means the sensor data is missing. [4.4]
You must verify the fault by comparing sensor values with independent local measurements. [14.2]
If the sensor is faulty, you should mark it as such and record the values. [13.4]
Only escalate if local checks confirm a real fault or if values reach alarm limits. [4.6]

PUMP-08|COMMUNICATION_LOSS.q: What do I check at the pump?
PUMP-08|COMMUNICATION_LOSS.a:
Check the pump locally for noise, vibration, and motor current [14.2].
Verify the sensor value against an independent measurement before trusting other alerts [4.4].
If the sensor is faulty, mark it as faulty and record before and after values [13.4].
Read local gauges every 2 hours and record the values until data returns [14.4].
Escalate to the chief engineer if a measured value reaches an alarm limit or a fault cannot be corrected [4.6].

PUMP-08|COMMUNICATION_LOSS.q: How do I restart the gateway?
PUMP-08|COMMUNICATION_LOSS.a: To restart the gateway, check its status light; if it is red, restart the gateway. [14.3]

PUMP-09|DISCHARGE_RESTRICTION.a:
You must check the positions of all discharge-side valves against the circuit diagram [7.2].
Verify these valves before performing any corrective work [4.3].
Do not change a valve position unless you know why it is in that position [7.2].
The minimum flow for normal operation is 100 m³/h [3.5]. Do not operate below this value for more than 10 minutes.

PUMP-09|DISCHARGE_RESTRICTION.q: When do I change over to the standby pump?
PUMP-09|DISCHARGE_RESTRICTION.a:
You must change over to the standby pump if the checks confirm a fault you cannot correct during operation [4.6].
You should also change over if any measured value reaches an alarm limit defined in Section 3 [4.6].
To perform the changeover, start the standby pump CW-1 and wait for stable discharge pressure [15.1].
Ensure the process cooling-water temperature remains within limits for 5 minutes before stopping PUMP-09 [15.2].
Finally, isolate PUMP-09 for work after the changeover is complete [15.3].

PUMP-09|AIR_ENTRAINMENT.q: How do I vent the pump?
PUMP-09|AIR_ENTRAINMENT.a: To vent the pump casing, open the vent cock [12.4]. Before doing this, you must stop the pump, lock out the motor supply, close and lock the suction and discharge valves, and release the pressure through the drain valve [2.1], [2.2]. Ensure the pressure gauge shows zero before opening the vent cock [2.2].

PUMP-09|AIR_ENTRAINMENT.q: What causes air in the water?
PUMP-09|AIR_ENTRAINMENT.a: Air in the water can be caused by a low basin level creating a vortex at the outlet, a leak in the suction pipe, or a foam problem in the basin [12.2].

PUMP-09|AIR_ENTRAINMENT.q: What do I do if the pump loses its prime?
PUMP-09|AIR_ENTRAINMENT.a: If the pump loses its prime, stop the pump and start the standby pump CW-1. [12.4]
